metadata.time_reference: All timestamps are seconds from the start of the original audio file.
warnings: Time signature could not be determined reliably; measure/downbeat fields are null.

tempo_curve.note: Raw frame-level tempo tracker output; the authoritative values are 'beats' and 'tempo_changes'.

intensity.description: Each value summarises [time, time + 1/sample_rate_hz). rms_normalized = RMS / 99th-percentile RMS (clipped 0..1); loudness_normalized maps 60 dB below the peak -> 0 and the peak -> 1.

limitations: Beat times come from onset-energy peaks (about +-12-25 ms accurate on clean transients); calibrate audio output latency separately in the game.
Tempo is tracked from rhythmic periodicity. Songs with weak or no percussion, heavy rubato, or long ambient sections give low-confidence beats (flagged via 'confidence'/'low_confidence').
Half-time / double-time cannot be resolved from audio alone; a tempo prior (start_bpm, min/max_bpm) picks the octave and 'octave_ambiguity_risk' flags segments outside 70-160 BPM.
Beat phase can lock onto off-beats in heavily syncopated music (the tracker follows the strongest periodic onsets, not 'musical beat' semantics).
Tempo changes are segmented from the tracked beats: sudden changes are located to within a few beats; gradual accelerations are reported as a staircase of small steps.
Meter is one global estimate with local bar-phase re-alignment. Mixed/changing time signatures are NOT labelled explicitly; they appear as phase slips (see warnings).
Downbeats are heuristic (bass onset + onset strength + harmonic change) and are the least reliable output; check 'time_signature.confidence' and per-beat 'meter_confidence'.
Subdivisions detect straight 8ths, triplets and 16ths only; swing/shuffle and polyrhythms are not recognised.

Beats inside silence or stretches with no onset activity (pauses, beatless intros, sustained pads) are removed rather than guessed; beats after a pause are marked 'after_pause'. See 'silences' and 'no_rhythmic_activity'.
